# The atlas of personas

13 people (10 clients, 3 staff), fictional composites built from the shop’s own product and the trade’s common knowledge. They are **hypotheses**: the independent research on barber-shop UX is thin and most of what is published comes from software vendors, so every claim below carries the class of its evidence and a way to test it on the salon’s own journal. The weights add up to 1 within each side and feed the persona view of the score; replace them with the shares you measure.

## How we know what we claim

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **O** | Observed in the product or its code: anyone can verify it |
| **J** | Validated on the salon’s own journal |
| **D** | Domain knowledge of the trade, not verified for this shop |
| **V** | Vendor-published claim: commercial interest, directional only |
| **H** | Hypothesis of the Cabinet: to be tested |

## Clients

### Le Fidèle · Sofiane, 34

*Logistics coordinator, lives in the 13th* · client · **core** · weight 25%

> « Le même que d’hab, dans trois semaines. »

Six years in the same chair, the same Thursday slot after work. He no longer describes his cut: he says « comme d’hab ». His loyalty is to a person, not to a shop: if his barber leaves, he leaves. He books with one thumb, from the tram or from the chair itself, and he notices within a second when something that used to work has moved.

**Why this weight.** Regulars are the base of a four-chair shop; every other persona is a regular in the making or a stranger on the way to one.
**Rhythm.** Every three weeks, same weekday, same hour (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “mon barbier”, “comme d’hab”, “le même”, “jeudi, après le taf”, “une place” · avoids: “prestation”, “formule”, “créer un compte”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 20 s · 4 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** M12 La prochaine · M13 Le retour · M04 Le créneau · M03 Le choix du barbier · M08 La veille

**Jobs to be done**
- Rebook the usual cut with the usual barber in two taps
- Be recognised: no re-typing, no “create an account”
- Know before he plans if his barber is away
- Move his slot when life moves, from the SMS, without phoning

**Fears**
- His barber fully booked, and being handed to a stranger without being asked
- A site that has forgotten him since last time
- A price that changed without warning
- Being nudged towards a membership he never asked for

**Delights**
- « Comme la dernière fois ? » as the first thing he sees
- His barber’s name on the confirmation
- A reminder with a link to move it
- The barber remembering last time’s note

**Success looks like.** Booked in under twenty seconds without typing a character; the confirmation names his barber.
**Failure looks like.** He is asked who he is again, or shown a stranger’s name. He phones, or he does not rebook.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: three or more visits with the same staffId at gaps clustered around 14–28 days; Clients › segment « fidèles »; a high « repris avant de partir » rate in Pilotage.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- « Comme la dernière fois ? » (the rebook card)
- Each barber shown by name with their next free time beside it
- The held slot: « Créneau gardé pour toi »

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `fidele.tram`: On the tram home, rebooking his usual. *Book the usual cut again as a returning client, three weeks out.*

| Scene | Moment | Device | Network | Scheme | Trials |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fidele.tram` | Wednesday 18:05 · on the tram home | Phone 390×844 (iPhone 14 class) | Fast 4G · 9 Mbps down · 150 ms | light | chrono |

**Evidence**

| Class | Claim | Where it can be observed | How to validate |
|---|---|---|---|
| D | Regulars return on a steady personal rhythm of about two to four weeks. |  | Clients › segments: the median gap between visits per client; expect clusters near 14, 21 and 28 days. |

### Le Nouveau · Yanis, 22

*Apprentice electrician, three weeks in Marseille* · client · **core** · weight 20%

> « Je veux pas me faire arnaquer, ni me faire raser la tête. »

He has a photo saved from Instagram and no words for it. On his lunch break he types « barbier près de moi », opens three tabs, and decides in the time it takes to eat a sandwich. He is not hunting for the best barber in Marseille; he wants the one that will not embarrass him, at a price he can read.

**Why this weight.** Every regular was a stranger once. The first impression is the acquisition funnel of a shop that lives on word of mouth and Google Maps.
**Rhythm.** One first visit; then every four to five weeks if it goes well (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “une coupe”, “un dégradé”, “c’est combien”, “y a de la place aujourd’hui ?”, “près de moi” · avoids: “sabot”, “tapering”, “formule premium”, “sur devis”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 60 s · 8 taps · 20 characters
**Moments.** M01 La vitrine · M02 La preuve · M03 Le choix du barbier · M09 La porte

**Jobs to be done**
- Judge quality in five seconds: real work, real people, a rating he can trust
- See the price before anything else
- Know if he can come now or soon, and how to get in
- Describe the cut without sounding clueless

**Fears**
- A bad cut he will wear for a month
- A price that grows at the till
- Being judged for not knowing the vocabulary
- Arriving at a closed door

**Delights**
- « Les prix, sans surprise. »
- « Sans préférence » presented as a normal answer
- « Un mot pour ton barbier » to say what he wants in his own words
- Photos that are clearly this shop’s

**Success looks like.** He knows where, how much and when within five seconds, and books without ever feeling stupid.
**Failure looks like.** He closes the tab and opens the next shop’s.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: first appointment, source « site » or Google; Clients › segment « nouveaux »; the first-visit no-show rate.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- The price in the main button (« Réserver · dès 15 € »)
- The live « Prochain créneau » on the hero
- The rating next to the address
- « Sans préférence · Le plus tôt » as the first choice

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `nouveau.rue`: Standing in the square at lunch, Google Maps in one hand, a weak signal. *Decide in five seconds whether to walk in or to book.*
- `nouveau.premiere`: His first booking, on the same phone, once he has decided. *Book a first cut as a stranger and know what it costs before committing.*

### Le Pressé · Julien, 41

*Sales director, sixty-hour weeks* · client · **core** · weight 18%

> « Donne-moi la prochaine place. N’importe quel barbier. »

He books his cut the way he books a train: late, in bed, in under a minute, or in a car park between two calls. He does not browse. He has no loyalty to a chair, only to the shop that makes it frictionless, and he will abandon on the first field he does not understand. He will never create an account.

**Why this weight.** The persona who most rewards a frictionless flow, and the one who punishes any ceremony. He is the stress test of the happy path.
**Rhythm.** Every three to four weeks, booked two to seven days ahead (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “dispo”, “le plus tôt”, “vendredi soir”, “n’importe qui”, “annuler” · avoids: “créer un compte”, “newsletter”, “choisir parmi onze”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 45 s · 6 taps · 20 characters
**Moments.** M04 Le créneau · M05 Les coordonnées · M07 La confirmation · M08 La veille

**Jobs to be done**
- The next available slot with anyone, in under forty-five seconds
- No account, the fewest possible fields
- A confirmation he can forward to his assistant
- Cancel by SMS link at 7 a.m. when a meeting moves

**Fears**
- A form longer than his patience
- A slot that disappears while he types
- Being forced to choose between things he has no opinion about
- A wall of text about deposits

**Delights**
- « Prochain créneau » on the home page
- « Sans préférence · Le plus tôt » as the first option
- The hold timer (he trusts the slot)
- The SMS with the move link

**Success looks like.** Booked in under forty-five seconds, five taps and a first name and a number.
**Failure looks like.** He backs out at the form, or at a choice he did not want to make.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: source « site », booking timestamp after 21:00, appointment within 7 days, no preferred barber.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- « Prochain créneau » on the home page
- « Sans préférence · Le plus tôt » and the « Le plus tôt · Choisir » shortcut
- Two required fields, the rest labelled « facultatif »
- The five-minute held slot, visible

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `presse.nuit`: 23:12 in bed, dark mode, one thumb, the shop is closed. *Book the earliest slot with anyone, then survive the keyboard and a dropped signal.*

| Scene | Moment | Device | Network | Scheme | Trials |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `presse.nuit` | Tuesday 23:12 · the shop is closed, a thumb is awake | Phone 390×844 (iPhone 14 class) | Fast 4G · 9 Mbps down · 150 ms | dark | chrono, nuit, clavier, tram, retour |

| V | Deposits cut no-shows sharply while costing few conversions (a vendor’s figures: 40–60% fewer no-shows, 3–5% fewer bookings). | https://bookedin.com/?p=16018 | Compare the no-show rate on the long services before and after the deposit (journal appt.noshow); needs weeks of data. |

### Le Parent · Nadia, 36

*Night-shift nurse; two sons (8 and 11) and a husband* · client · **growth** · weight 9%

> « Trois têtes à faire, une seule soirée de libre. »

The person who books is not the person who sits in the chair. She plans on Sunday evening with an iPad on her knees, interrupted every ninety seconds. She wants the boys one after the other, or with two barbers at once, and one text to say so. Every flow built for one person costs her three bookings and a good deal of goodwill.

**Why this weight.** The booker is not the client: each parent is two or three clients at once, and the gap is structural, not cosmetic.
**Rhythm.** Each child every four to six weeks, the father every three (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “les garçons”, “mon mari et mes fils”, “à la suite”, “pour mon fils” · avoids: “un seul client par réservation”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 120 s · 14 taps · 50 characters
**Moments.** M03 Le choix du barbier · M04 Le créneau · M05 Les coordonnées · M07 La confirmation

**Jobs to be done**
- Book two or three people back to back, in one go
- Know the price and the time of each (a child’s cut is shorter)
- One confirmation, one SMS, one link to move them all
- Put the tablet down for five minutes and find everything where she left it

**Fears**
- Booking three separate appointments on three different days
- A barber with no patience for an eight-year-old
- Losing the form when a child shouts
- A hold timer that expires mid-argument

**Delights**
- « Ajouter une personne » (it does not exist yet)
- A suggestion of consecutive slots
- A child’s price stated plainly
- One reminder that lists everyone

**Success looks like.** Two people booked back to back in one sitting, one confirmation for both.
**Failure looks like.** She books one, forgets the other, and phones.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: pairs of appointments by different clients on the same booking phone, within ten minutes of each other, same day.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- The held slot and its visible timer
- Nothing typed lost when the screen is left

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `parent.dimanche`: Sunday 20:30 on the sofa, an iPad, interrupted every ninety seconds. *Book a father and his son back to back; be interrupted for six minutes and come back.*

### L’Occasion · Théo, 27

*Wedding witness, Saturday* · client · **growth** · weight 7%

> « Samedi, c’est le grand jour. Je dois être irréprochable. »

Once or twice a year something happens (a wedding, an interview, a new job, a break-up) and he wants a different head. He has the most to lose, spends the most and reads everything. For him a clear deposit rule and a named diagnostic are reassurance, not friction.

**Why this weight.** The highest ticket per visit (Transformation 50 €, Silver 100 €) and the likeliest to tell the story afterwards.
**Rhythm.** Once or twice a year, with a hard deadline (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “décoloration”, “blond”, “pour un mariage”, “c’est faisable ?”, “combien de temps ça prend” · avoids: “frais de dossier”, “pénalité”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 120 s · 9 taps · 25 characters
**Moments.** M02 La preuve · M04 Le créneau · M06 La garantie · M07 La confirmation

**Jobs to be done**
- Secure the right transformation slot before Friday
- Understand what is included and how long it really takes
- Understand the deposit: how much, why, what if he cancels
- See that the shop has done this before

**Fears**
- An irreversible colour result
- No slot left by Thursday
- Losing a deposit he did not understand
- Not being heard: nobody to ask

**Delights**
- « Diagnostic · Étude de faisabilité · Coupe » in plain words
- A deposit line that says why, once
- « Un mot pour ton barbier »
- Before-and-after photos of similar work

**Success looks like.** He books the right service, understands the deposit before the button, and trusts the slot.
**Failure looks like.** He discovers the deposit at the payment step and feels trapped.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: Transformation, Décoloration or Silver booked within seven days of the appointment; deposit paid.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- The service names that say what is included
- The deposit line before the confirm button

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `occasion.lundi`: Monday 21:00, the wedding is Saturday and the shop is closed. *Book a Transformation and understand the deposit before paying.*

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Le Passionné · Mehdi, 19

*Student, plays football, follows barbers on Instagram* · client · **growth** · weight 8%

> « C’est qui qui fait les dégradés à blanc ici ? »

He knows the names of the fade styles and of the barbers who invented them. He reads a barbershop’s site the way a designer reads a portfolio: the photography, the type, how it moves. He books a barber, not a shop; if the site looks like a template, he assumes the cuts do too. He is also the one who shares: his story on Friday night is the shop’s best advertising.

**Why this weight.** Small revenue, large reach: the ambassador, and the toughest design critic who will ever open the site.
**Rhythm.** Every two to three weeks, to keep the fade sharp (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “fade”, “skin fade”, “dégradé à blanc”, “le barber”, “le rendu” · avoids: “coupe homme classique”, “formule”, “prestation”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 90 s · 6 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** M01 La vitrine · M02 La preuve · M03 Le choix du barbier

**Jobs to be done**
- See each barber’s hand: portfolio, specialty, Instagram
- Book that barber, and nobody else
- Feel that the shop has taste, in motion, photography and copy
- Share a booking or a result without friction

**Fears**
- Stock photography
- A slow, heavy, over-animated page
- Marketing language
- Not being able to tell who does what

**Delights**
- Real work in the gallery
- A barber’s name that opens onto their hand and their Instagram
- Motion with a point
- A moment worth sharing

**Success looks like.** He thinks « ils savent ce qu’ils font », follows a barber and books.
**Failure looks like.** He decides it is a template and goes where his friends go.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: a named barber chosen, age under 25, frequent short-gap visits; the note field names a style.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- Real photography of the shop’s own work
- Motion that respects reduced-motion
- Self-hosted fonts and no third-party requests

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `passionne.vendredi`: Friday 17:00 on a laptop, scrolling slowly, judging. *Judge the craft: type, motion, photography, performance.*

### L’Ancien · Gérard, 67

*Retired technician, grandfather of three* · client · **edge** · weight 5%

> « Je préfère téléphoner, mais montrez-moi comment faire. »

His grandson showed him the site. He has had his hair cut by someone he knew for thirty years and is wary of anything that needs a screen. His eyes tire at small grey text, and his thumb is wider than the icon. He needs to see that it worked (the day, the hour and the barber in words) and a number to call if it did not.

**Why this weight.** A small share, but the persona that exposes every shortcut in accessibility, and the grandfather who brings three generations through the door.
**Rhythm.** Every four weeks, mornings (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “le salon”, “prendre rendez-vous”, “mardi prochain”, “le matin”, “téléphoner” · avoids: “icônes sans mots”, “compte à rebours”, “jargon”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 180 s · 10 taps · 20 characters
**Moments.** M01 La vitrine · M07 La confirmation · M08 La veille · M09 La porte · M14 La sortie

**Jobs to be done**
- Find the opening hours and a phone number at once
- Read everything without squinting or zooming
- Never make an irreversible mistake with a tap
- Keep a confirmation he can show or reread

**Fears**
- Tapping the wrong thing
- A countdown that makes him feel rushed
- Icons without words
- Being treated as a problem

**Delights**
- Large, plain type
- A phone number that dials on tap
- A confirmation in full words
- A person answering at the shop

**Success looks like.** He finds a number or books, and holds a confirmation he can read aloud.
**Failure looks like.** He cannot find how to reach a person, so he walks in or does not come.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: source « phone » or « walkin », age over 60 (birth date is kept for birthdays); interviews with three clients over sixty.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- Plain labels on controls
- Nothing breaks at 320 px
- The cancellation page reachable from every footer

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `ancien.jeudi`: Thursday 10:00, large print, looking for a phone number. *Find the hours and a number to call; read without squinting; book without a mistake.*

### L’Abonné · Maxime, 29

*Field technician, always on the road* · client · **growth** · weight 4%

> « Je paye pour ne plus y penser. »

He pays monthly so that a cut is never an event. He wants to know how many are left, when the next charge is, and that he can stop whenever he wants without a conversation. He measures the shop by how little it asks of him, and by how it behaves on the day he leaves.

**Why this weight.** Recurring revenue, and the only persona with a legal right to leave that the product already honours.
**Rhythm.** Every week or two, on his own day (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “mon abonnement”, “ma coupe de la semaine”, “résilier”, “prélèvement” · avoids: “engagement”, “période de rétractation (unexplained)”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 30 s · 5 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** M04 Le créneau · M14 La sortie

**Jobs to be done**
- Book with no payment friction
- Know the cuts left and the next charge
- Understand the rule in plain words (lost, month, free)
- Cancel with dignity

**Fears**
- Paying for cuts he cannot use
- A lock-in he cannot undo
- A rule he understood only after losing a cut
- An unexplained charge

**Delights**
- « Réservé avec ton abonnement : rien n’est demandé en ligne »
- A member page that says what is left
- An honest, one-tap cancellation
- The rule said in words

**Success looks like.** He cancels in a few taps and is told exactly what happens next.
**Failure looks like.** He is made to justify himself, or cannot find the door.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: Clients › Abonnés; the cancellation rate and the reason field; the 14-day withdrawals.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- « Résilier mon abonnement » in every footer
- The member page’s plain-words rule
- « Renoncer au contrat ici » for the 14-day right

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `abonne.sortie`: He wants out: from the footer, on his phone, with no account. *Find how to cancel his membership and understand what happens next.*

| Scene | Moment | Device | Network | Scheme | Trials |

### Le Cadeau · Camille, 31

*Buys for her father’s birthday; has never set foot in the shop* · client · **edge** · weight 2%

> « Je veux offrir quelque chose de beau, sans me tromper. »

She is not a client; she is a gift-giver buying for someone who is. She needs to choose an amount, add a few words and have it arrive in minutes, looking like a gift and not a voucher. She comes twice a year (Father’s Day, Christmas) and is the cheapest customer the shop will ever acquire.

**Why this weight.** Small and seasonal, but a gift card is a new client who arrives already persuaded by someone they trust.
**Rhythm.** Twice a year, around Father’s Day and Christmas (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “une carte cadeau”, “pour mon père”, “offrir”, “bon d’achat” · avoids: “bon d’achat anonyme”, “frais cachés”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 120 s · 8 taps · 80 characters
**Moments.** M02 La preuve · M07 La confirmation

**Jobs to be done**
- Choose an amount and a message in under two minutes
- Have it arrive at once and look beautiful
- Know how it will be used and how long it lasts
- Pay once, with trust, a shop she has never seen

**Fears**
- A cheap-looking voucher
- Choosing the wrong amount
- The recipient not knowing how to use it
- A shop she cannot judge

**Delights**
- A preview of the card
- Amounts tied to real services
- Instant delivery
- A personal message

**Success looks like.** She buys, sees the card, and knows exactly what her father will receive.
**Failure looks like.** She is unsure what he gets, and buys flowers instead.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: gift-card sales by month (Catalogue › Cartes cadeaux); redemptions by first-time clients.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- A four-step order with one button
- Self-hosted fonts on the gift page too

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `cadeau.soir`: A weekday evening on a phone, buying for her father. *Buy a gift card and know it worked.*

### Le Futur Barbier · Nassim, 18

*Wants to become a barber; his mother reads over his shoulder* · client · **edge** · weight 2%

> « Je veux apprendre le dégradé, pas regarder des vidéos. »

He has practised on his friends for two years. He has found that the shop is an approved training centre, and he wants three answers: what it costs, when, and whether it leads to a diploma. His mother wants the same answers in writing, and a person to talk to.

**Why this weight.** A different business line (training, quoted) with a different funnel (an enquiry form): small volume, high margin.
**Rhythm.** A single enquiry, once, with a long decision (hypothesis)
**His words.** says: “formation”, “apprendre”, “stage”, “diplôme”, “agrément” · avoids: “sur devis (without a range)”, “sur demande (without a date)”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 120 s · 6 taps · 200 characters
**Moments.** M01 La vitrine · M02 La preuve

**Jobs to be done**
- Know the modules, who teaches, the cost and the dates
- Know whether it is certified
- Ask a question and be answered by a person
- See the work of the people who would teach him

**Fears**
- A scam school
- « Sur devis » meaning « trop cher pour le dire »
- Silence after he sends his details
- Not being taken seriously at eighteen

**Delights**
- Named modules with real content
- « Salon formateur agréé » with a proof
- A short form with a promised reply time
- A visible human

**Success looks like.** He knows what, whether certified, and how to ask; the form promises a reply.
**Failure looks like.** He cannot tell what it costs or when, and does not write.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: the enquiries inbox (Réglages › Demandes); the share that mention a diploma or an apprenticeship.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- Named modules with real content
- « Titulaire d’un agrément de formateur » stated up front

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `futur.formations`: After class, on a phone, with his mother. *Understand the training offer and ask a question.*

## Staff

### Le Barbier au fauteuil · Anis, 26

*Barber, six years in the trade* · staff · **core** · weight 50%

> « J’ai les mains pleines. Donne-moi le client suivant, rien d’autre. »

Twenty-five to forty-five minutes under a client’s eyes, hands wet, gloved or full of product. Between two clients he has sixty to ninety seconds: glance at who is next and what he had last time, tap « Il est là », tap « Au fauteuil ». He shares a tablet with three colleagues and never wants a client to read another client’s notes, or the till’s money. Software that makes him look slow in front of a client is software he stops using.

**Why this weight.** Four chairs, four barbers: the people whose hands touch the product the most, and the ones who decide whether it lives or dies on the floor.
**Rhythm.** A client every thirty to forty-five minutes, nine to eighteen thirty, five days
**His words.** says: “mon prochain”, “il est là”, “au fauteuil”, “la note” · avoids: “paramètres”, “rapport”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 10 s · 2 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** S02 Le coup de feu · M10 Le fauteuil

**Jobs to be done**
- See the next client and the last cut’s note at a glance
- Change a status with one big tap
- Write a cut note in ten seconds
- See his own numbers, privately
- Sign in on a shared device in a few seconds

**Fears**
- The screen locking mid-cut
- A client reading money or other clients’ notes
- Targets too small for a wet thumb
- A network drop eating a note

**Delights**
- « Il est là » and « Au fauteuil » as the two biggest things on screen
- « La dernière fois » written by a colleague
- Amounts hidden until he asks
- A big, calm PIN keypad

**Success looks like.** Signed in in six taps, the next client and last time’s note on the first screen, status in one tap.
**Failure looks like.** He hunts for the next client, mis-taps, or a client reads the screen.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: status changes per appointment and their latency; cut notes written per barber; the lock events.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- The PIN keypad’s large keys
- The two big status buttons
- Amounts hidden by default on a shared device
- « La dernière fois » on the next-client card

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `barbier.fauteuil`: Between two clients, wet hands, a shared phone propped at the station. *Sign in with a PIN, see the next client, mark him arrived.*

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `barbier.fauteuil` | Tuesday 15:10 · a busy afternoon (the demo salon's own clock) | Phone 390×844 (iPhone 14 class) | wifi | dark | mains |

| Class | Claim | Where it can be observed | How to validate |

### L’Accueil · Lina, 23

*Front desk: the phone, the door and the till at once* · staff · **core** · weight 30%

> « Quatre choses en même temps, et il faut que ça tienne. »

She is the shop’s router: a phone ringing, a walk-in at the door, a client at the till, a barber asking if his 15:30 has arrived. Every screen she uses is glanced at, not read. She forgives a lot, but not a wrong tap on money or a dialog that swallows what she was doing.

**Why this weight.** The one person who touches every screen in a day, under pressure, with a client watching.
**Rhythm.** Eight hours of interruptions; the Saturday rush is the real test
**His words.** says: “je le mets en caisse”, “il est arrivé”, “il est en retard”, “décale-le” · avoids: “paramétrer”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 30 s · 6 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** S01 L’ouverture · S02 Le coup de feu · M11 La caisse · M12 La prochaine

**Jobs to be done**
- Add a walk-in in two taps
- Move an appointment (the client is texted automatically)
- Check a client out in under thirty seconds
- See at a glance who is here, late, free

**Fears**
- A mis-tap on an amount or a refund
- A double booking
- Dialogs stacked on dialogs
- Losing her place after an interruption

**Delights**
- « P » for Passage; ⌘K to search anything
- « À encaisser » with the chair status
- A toast with an undo
- A till that deducts the deposit by itself

**Success looks like.** Checkout in under thirty seconds, every control hittable at a glance.
**Failure looks like.** A secondary action the size of a text link causes a mis-tap on money.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: the time from « terminé » to « encaissé » per ticket; refunds and credit notes; undo toasts used.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- The « à encaisser » list
- Deposits and memberships deducted automatically
- Undo on every reversible action

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `accueil.coupdefeu`: Saturday 09:40 at the desk: the opening rush, a tablet in landscape, a client at the till. *Check out a finished client and move around the agenda without a mis-tap.*

### Le Gérant · Rachid, 45

*Owner and barber; does the numbers at night* · staff · **core** · weight 20%

> « Dis-moi si le mois tient, et si mes gars sont payés juste. »

He is a barber first and a business owner second, and the second job happens at 23:00 on a laptop or a phone with a cold coffee. He wants one answer (is the month on track?) in five seconds, and the proof behind it when his accountant asks. He is wary of anything he cannot audit, and of anything that exposes the shop’s money to a client’s eyes.

**Why this weight.** He signs the product’s cheque, and he is the only persona who reads it as a business, not as a tool.
**Rhythm.** Every evening, ten minutes; the month’s end, an hour
**His words.** says: “le mois”, “l’objectif”, “les gars”, “la clôture”, “le comptable” · avoids: “paramétrage”, “module”
**Budget (what the trials hold the product to).** 5 s · 0 taps · 0 characters
**Moments.** S03 La clôture · S04 Le soir

**Jobs to be done**
- The month’s status against the goal in five seconds
- Cash certainty: the till’s Z, sealed
- Commission fairness for each barber
- No-shows and deposits at a glance
- Exports for the accountant without spreadsheet gymnastics

**Fears**
- A compliance fine (the certified-till rule)
- A number he cannot explain
- Complexity creeping in
- Staff seeing the shop’s money

**Delights**
- Pilotage’s tiles with a goal and a projection
- The journal’s integrity proof
- Privacy mode: amounts hidden
- Rules written in plain words

**Success looks like.** He knows whether the month holds before he finishes his coffee.
**Failure looks like.** Twelve tiles and no verdict; or a number he cannot trace.
**How to spot them in the salon’s data.** Journal: the owner’s sessions by hour; exports run; the Z closures and their gaps.

**Protect (never break for them)**
- Pilotage’s goal and projection
- The journal’s integrity proof
- Privacy mode for amounts

**Scenes the harness runs**

- `gerant.soir`: 23:00 on a laptop, dark theme, a cold coffee, checking the month. *See if the month is on track in five seconds.*
